Q. 1 غَرْقَأَتْ , said of an egg (بَيْضَةٌ), It came forth having upon it [only] its thin integument [or pellicle, called غِرْقِئ]. (K.) ―
-b2- And, said of a hen, [in the K in art. غرق [in which the hemzeh is said to be augmentative) غرقأت بَيْضَهَا] She laid her eggs in the state described above. (K.) [But see what follows.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
